coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Domestic service minimum wage P1,500/month from 1 Feb 2024 (S.I. 7 of 2024, per WageIndicator). No employer registration or filing duty found; nothing recurring for an authority. Weak.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Council bye-laws (e.g. Central District Council Scrap Metal and Scrap Yard Control Bye-laws S.I. 7 of 2010): dealer licence P200, licence names scrapyards and metals, mandatory register of sellers/metals/prices. Export of scrap needs Ministry registration (S.I. 153 of 2014). Candidate C01.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No Botswana second-hand dealer or pawnbroker statute or register found; Trade Regulations 2008 list shows no such category (unverified). Nothing new.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Precious and Semi-Precious Stones (Protection) Act: dealer licences via Minister / Dept of Mines (semi-precious dealer licence service on gov.bw). Nothing found on gold or a jewellery register. Not enough to judge.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No dismantler or spare-parts rules found. Motor Dealer Licence (new/used) is issued by DRTS, fee about P1,690 per gov.bw (undated). Finance Minister said in March 2025 that grey used-vehicle imports are a major non-compliance source. Candidate C08 weak.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K10 (not re-searched, per contract).

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Livestock and Meat Industries Act Cap 36:03; Red Meat Abattoir Regs S.I. 56/2007 and Poultry Abattoir Regs S.I. 55/2007 cover abattoir and cutting-premises licences. A butchery needs a Trade Act fresh-produce licence (citizen-reserved). No small-butcher recurring filing found.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No beekeeper registry or permit found. A 2025 review says there is no legal framework for the sub-sector. National Apiculture Strategy runs to 2027. Importation of Bees Act is old. Nothing to build on.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Diseases of Animals Act s.16 permit to sell, manufacture or import vet medicines (2017 source). BOMRA runs vet product registration and exemptions. No recurring seller register or return found. Candidate C09 weak.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Drillers hold Ministry of Trade licences (Minister's 2023 statement). Borehole Completion Certificate, Form GS 184 and borehole registry are run by the Dept of Water and Sanitation. Water rights go to the Water Apportionment Board. The Water Act and Borehole Act were said to be under review. Candidate C07 weak.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Waste Management Act Cap 65:06 s.12-13: waste carrier licence for moving controlled waste, plus a facility licence valid one year. Unclear whether septage is controlled waste. The gov.bw page returned 503 when fetched. Candidate C06 weak.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Factories Act 1973 s.37(7): steam boilers examined at least every 14 months by a DOHS-authorised examiner. Report kept on site. Provisions for lifts (s.31), cranes (s.33) and a lifting-tackle register (s.34). Candidate C03.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Budget used on other categories; no search run.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Agrochemicals Act 18 of 1999 s.15: licence to import, sell or distribute (Form 7, P200); product registration includes fertilisers. Fertiliser sold unregistered is an offence (2014 warning). Candidate C05 weak.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Employment Act Part V: recruiter licence (Type A P20, Type B P100) and individual recruiter permits from the Dept of Labour. Renewals need quarterly returns of employees recruited per district. Candidate C02.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Council cemetery bye-laws require burial permits and a burial register kept by the council. No national funeral-parlour licensing found. Burial societies fall under the Societies Act (K05).

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Societies (Amendment) Act 5 of 2025 in force 24 Jan 2025 (SI 1/2025): new s.4, 4B, 29B-D; Registrar must verify controllers' identity; two-thirds of office-bearers must reside in Botswana. Electronic re-registration closed 24 Feb 2024; annual returns carry a P50 charge. About 10,000 societies. Same buyer and duty as K05. Candidate C04 known K05.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Road Transport (Permits) Cap 69:03 via DRTS: taxi, call-cab and minibus permits are reserved for citizens; renewal needs the expired permit and token, listed at 39 working days; vehicle inspection certificate needed; call cabs need a BOCRA radio licence. Candidate C10.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Hawking and street vending are licensed by council bye-laws (1985-2010 versions). Bureaux de change are licensed by the Bank of Botswana under Bank of Botswana (Bureaux de Change) Regulations 2004, with about 60 operating at end-2020 and some licences revoked. Candidate C11.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Day-care centres are licensed by council bye-laws with 12-month licences. Driving school permit is BWP 390 with BWP 260 renewal, and instructor certificates renew annually (gov.bw). Tattoo, food-producer and hunting rules not searched. Candidates C12 and C13.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: BERA licenses retail stations, LPG and storage. BERA statement dated 17-18 June 2026: nationwide enforcement since May 2026, six filling stations temporarily shut for environmental and safety breaches (missing or non-working oil-water separators). Petroleum Products Regulations 2024 cited by BERA; a 2018 draft is also on its site (version in force unconfirmed). The statement PDF could not be read by WebFetch, so details come from search snippets. No Botswana station-compliance software found (competitor search not run).

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Control of Maize Milling Act: commercial and restricted miller licences expire 31 December each year (fees in the schedule look dated). BAMB holds the statutory purchase role for grain; 2023 directive restricted grain import and export. No 2026 licensing change found. Small niche, nothing strong.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Co-operative Societies Act (Cap 42:04, 1964 base): registration, annual accounts and audit reports go to the Commissioner for Co-operative Development. NBFIRA regulates non-bank lenders and may cover lending activity. No filing portal or software found. Close to K05 in shape (society annual returns) but a different buyer group.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: Ministry of Health Private Practice Licensing Office issues annual licences (Guidelines MOH PPL GLN V2, May 2024). The 2025/26 renewal opened 5 May, and only 28 labs had renewed by 18 July 2025. Private practice renewal form is a downloadable PDF with no online portal mentioned. BOMAID requires claims within 120 days and pre-authorisation for listed services; it is rolling out a provider self-service claims platform. Government owes private providers a large arrears amount (2025 medicine shortage emergency). No Botswana practice-management product found; the South African products GoodX and NetPractice do not mention Botswana.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: BoMRA regulates under the Medicines and Related Substances Act. Act 29 of 2025 continues BoMRA (commencement unconfirmed). BoMRA standalone-pharmacy licensing guideline carries an effective date of 15 April 2026. Separate registers are required for each scheduled-medicine category and for precursor chemicals; import and export need a BoMRA application. Not enough to judge a software gap.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Private Security Services Act: licensing board, annual licence renewal, citizen-director rule, BURS tax compliance check. Employment-law non-compliance (wages, deductions) is documented in the sector. Cleaning services is a citizen-reserved trade licence. Nothing beyond K04. No 2024 Act found.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Public Procurement Act 2021, PPRA registration through IPMS, and section 76 reservations for 100% citizen-owned firms. Citizen economic empowerment and local-procurement schemes appear in tender evaluation (BERA tenders). I could not confirm any 'Citizen Economic Empowerment Act 2025'. Nothing new beyond K03 and K08.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Financial Intelligence Act 2022 (in force 25 Feb 2022), goAML registration through FIA. A Financial Intelligence (Amendment) Bill was reported passed in August 2026 (assent and commencement unconfirmed). FIA risk notice of 23 Feb 2026 on enhanced due diligence. CIPA beneficial-ownership duty under the Companies (Amendment) Act 2019. Nothing new beyond K02.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Tourism Act (Cap 42:09) and Botswana Tourism Organisation Regulations (S.I. 47 of 2010): tourist enterprise licence, mandatory grading (offence of operating ungraded carries up to P20,000 and/or 5 years), annual grading renewal. Domestic guesthouse guidelines list ongoing duties: monthly Training Levy returns, monthly accommodation statistics, guest register, residents-only alcohol sales. Not covered by any known idea. No Botswana software found for these returns.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: DFRR veldt-product permits (harvester, dealer, exporter; the dealer and exporter permits are valid 30 days; exporter fee P500 for citizens). Hides and Skins Export Act needs a permit per consignment. No traceability scheme found for charcoal, timber or mophane worms. Small-volume permit work, not a recurring filing.

coverage.category: 31. Liquor licensees (bars, bottle stores, depots, nightclubs)
coverage.found: Liquor Act: licence renewal on Form 4 with P100 fee; one licence per location; bar, bottle store, depot and nightclub licences are reserved for citizens. Applications need annual returns, premises proof and zoning validation. March 2026 news: a Liquor Act amendment bill would abolish liquor control authorities, introduce online licensing, and drop highway and church distance buffers; Kanye councillors rejected it. coverage.category: 32. Trade licence holders at district councils (general dealers, car washes, cleaning, auctioneers)
coverage.found: Trade Act (Cap 43:02): licences are issued by district councils, renewed on the anniversary date, with the latest company annual returns as a renewal document. Some licences are reserved for citizens. A 2019 Trade Bill proposing a move to a 'positive' licence list has unknown status. Older Trade Act provision on import and export returns may still apply (unconfirmed).

coverage.category: 33. Companies on the CIPA register (annual returns and beneficial ownership)
coverage.found: Annual returns are due in the incorporation month; non-filing risks removal from the register (a 2017 report gives P900 penalty plus P300 annual fee; current schedule unconfirmed). Beneficial-ownership duty exists under the Companies (Amendment) Act 2019. Law firms and accountants (PwC, Andersen, RSM) sell company secretarial services. No self-serve tool found.

coverage.category: 34. Gambling licensees (betting shops, limited payout machines, casinos)
coverage.found: Gambling Authority issued the first betting licences (10) and limited payout machine licences (6) after a 2023 call. Machine registration and electronic monitoring system exist in the Act. Operators are few and mostly large or foreign. Weak for a solo founder.

coverage.category: 35. Veldt product harvesters, dealers and exporters
coverage.found: DFRR permits: harvester (citizens 18+, Omang), dealer and exporter, 30-day validity, 3-day processing. Mophane worms not named on the permit pages (unconfirmed). Low value per client.

coverage.category: 36. Public procurement bidders (PPRA registration, citizen-reserved tenders)
coverage.found: Registration of bidders through PPRA IPMS, with section 76 reservations for 100% citizen-owned firms. Overlaps K03 on the buyer side, so counted as known.

coverage.category: 37. Tourist enterprise licensees: lodges, camps, safari operators (HRDC training levy and statistics returns)
coverage.found: Monthly Training Levy returns and accommodation statistics named in domestic guesthouse guidelines; grading and licence renewals under BTO. Covered with category 29.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: No recurring licensing or reporting duty found for small or private water systems in Botswana, so nothing strong. Water supply is centralised on the Water Utilities Corporation (WUC, 1970 Act) and the Department of Water and Sanitation (DWS). The Water Act (Cap 34:01, 1968) and Borehole Act (Cap 34:02) are still the operative laws. In July 2023 the minister acknowledged gaps in both and said they were under review through the World Bank-funded BEWSE project. A 2020 Centre for Applied Research (CAR) review of water legislation and a possible water regulatory authority was found, but I saw no evidence of a tabled bill or of a regulator being set up (2018 plan only). Drinking-water quality standard is BOS 32:2015, tested by WUC and the DWS labs in Gaborone and Maun. Rural, community and private supplies are weakly covered. Village and community boreholes are run by community associations, described in 2018 as 'dysfunctional', or by councils. The few recurring filings found are in category 10 territory: borehole completion certificate (Form G.S. 184, free, one day) and the water rights application (BWP 60, 90 days, needs a borehole certificate, Omang, land papers and a Director of Lands letter). These are one-off per borehole and the buyer group is farmers and landholders, not a quiet regulated trade. Bottled water and water-refill stations: BOBS compulsory standards BOS 143 and BOS 262 (2023 editions notified to the WTO; whether in force is unverified); producer-level certification only. I found no permit regime for water kiosks, vendors or bowsers. Tourism lodges in the Okavango run own borehole and septic systems; discharge permitting is ambiguous (waste-facility licences sit with the Department of Waste Management and Pollution Control, which must consult DWS). Could not check: any Water Bill in Parliament in 2025-2026, whether a water regulator now exists, current water-rights holder reporting or charges, and the current WUC tariff and sub-metering rules for resellers and landlords.
